messages.text: Merson: Arsenal didn't make X-factor signing to win Champions League

metadata.summary: Arsenal's record last year was amazing in the Champions League and they're going to be there or thereabouts again – but I don't think they bought that X factor signing to take them to that next level.
metadata.content: Arsenal didn't make X factor signing like Vinicius Junior or Julian Alvarez to win Champions League, says Paul Merson | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Arsenal didn't make X factor signing like Vinicius Junior or Julian Alvarez to win Champions League, says Paul Merson Paul Merson gives his verdict on Arsenal's Champions League hopes in his latest column; Sky Sports pundit believes Gunners needed more than Kai Havertz up front; Follow Napoli vs Arsenal on the Sky Sports app with our dedicated match commentary from 6.30pm on Wednesday Paul Merson Football Expert & Columnist @PaulMerse Wednesday 9 September 2026 15:58, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Merson has his say on whether Arsenal will have a chance at claiming Champions League glory. Arsenal's record last year was amazing in the Champions League and they're going to be there or thereabouts again – but I don't think they bought that X factor signing to take them to that next level. They have enough to win the Premier League with their squad. I just think the forward line against the big boys, they're missing that little ingredient. If they'd had a Vinicius Junior or a Julian Alvarez, that would have given them the edge to go on and win the Champions League. I think they might just fall short. Antonelli joined the Mercedes junior programme as an 11-year-old after some remarkable results in karting and quickly rose up the motorsport ranks to Formula 1 and replaced Lewis Hamilton at the Silver Arrows only last year. He currently leads the Drivers' Championship by 66 points from team-mate George Russell ahead of this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid and is on course to become the youngest world champion in F1 history at 20 years old. metadata.content: Solheim Cup 2026: Nelly Korda plays down 'intimidation factor' to Team Europe as Charley Hull eyes rematch with world No 1 | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content Solheim Cup 2026: Nelly Korda plays down 'intimidation factor' to Team Europe as Charley Hull eyes rematch with world No 1 Nelly Korda headlines Team USA at the Solheim Cup, who look to retain the trophy in the Netherlands; Charley Hull makes her eighth consecutive appearance for Team Europe; watch Solheim Cup live on Friday from 6am on Sky Sports Golf By Ali Stafford at Bernardus Golf Wednesday 9 September 2026 16:16, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charley Hull gave a funny answer when asked about her possible Solheim Cup playing partner Charley Hull said she would relish another Solheim Cup showdown with Nelly Korda, who played down bringing an "intimidation factor" to Team Europe. Hull makes an eighth consecutive Solheim Cup appearance for Team Europe, who look to regain the trophy at Bernardus Golf - live on Sky Sports - after losing on American soil two years ago. The 30-year-old top-scored for Team Europe in their 2024 defeat and despatched Korda 6&4 during the Sunday singles, with Hull open to facing the world No 1 again for Anna Nordqvist's side during their pursuit of a home victory. messages.text: Shelton beats Alcaraz at 3.33am in New York epic

metadata.summary: Ben Shelton clinched the biggest win of his career as he defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set epic stretching deep into the New York night to reach the semi-finals of the US Open.
metadata.content: US Open: Ben Shelton beats Carlos Alcaraz in five-set thriller in latest-ever finish to US Open match at 3.33am | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to content US Open: Ben Shelton beats Carlos Alcaraz in five-set thriller in latest-ever finish to US Open match at 3.33am Ben Shelton clinches first-ever victory over top-three opponent as he beats Carlos Alcaraz to set up US Open semi-final showdown with Frances Tiafoe; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app Wednesday 9 September 2026 12:37, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the thrilling US Open quarter-final between Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz Ben Shelton clinched the biggest win of his career as he defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in a five-set epic stretching deep into the New York night to reach the semi-finals of the US Open. The American prevailed 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 (10-7) over four hours and 28 minutes to reward a raucous Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd gripped until 3.33am in what was the latest-ever finish to a US Open match. It marked Shelton's first career win over a top-three player, against which he had been 0-17 coming into the match. Shelton will now play Frances Tiafoe in the final four after his fellow countryman's thrilling five-set victory over Alex Michelsen earlier in the evening.
